The adults are not timid about anything: they eat cloth, wool first and then any natural fibre, worn or stored, and settle for grass only when nothing better is within reach. A tamed one can be shorn of a fine moth-silk, the fungal felt of its wings, provided the silk is kept well away from every other dustveil, which will eat that too. It is NOT an Earth animal: wings made of a felt of fungal threads instead of scaled membrane; wings dusted with spores; wings hang from the body like a veil. observed.facings.png: A tan-brown mammal with a deer or gazelle fawn's head, big pointed ears, short fur and a tufted tail, on four extremely long stilt legs with ball-like knee joints and small cloven hooves. South shows the face toward the camera, east is a side profile facing right, and north shows the rump, tail and back of the head. All three are about the same height.
observed.south.png: Front view: a fawn-like face with two large dark eyes, a dark nose and wide ears. The chest is rounded and pale. The front leg pair stands wide, with the rear pair behind and between it. A dark tail tuft hangs under the belly between the legs. The background is clean.
observed.east.png: Side profile: a long slim antelope torso with mottled brown striping on the back, a neck reaching forward, a doe's head with a large dark eye, and a dark tufted tail. Four very thin legs, roughly four to five times the torso depth, have knobbly mid-joints and cloven hooves.
observed.north.png: Rear view: pale rump, dark tail hanging down the centre, dark stripe along the spine, and the back of the head with two ears. No eyes or face. Four thin legs end in cloven hooves.
observed.scale.png: Beside the human, the belly sits about level with or just above the top of the human's head, and the legs are about two cells long. At 32 px per cell it reads as a small tan deer body on four hair-thin dark legs. The body's tan is close to the sand colour.

request.subject: RM_Harrok

edits.change: The head is an invented ambusher's head: a long, earless, elongated skull with a narrow beak-like jaw, small sunken dark eyes set low on the sides, and no fur muzzle or wet nose. The hide is bare, leathery and slightly plated in dull sand-grey and ochre, with no fur, no tufted tail and no cloven hooves. Each of the four thin legs ends in a splayed, spike-like foot with three long toes that grip the sand.

The long neck hangs low and still, bending down from the high narrow torso so the narrow jaw rests just above the sand beneath the body. The jaw is built to pluck small animals from the shadowed ground below, and the pose is a motionless ambush, with the head pointed down and the eyes watching the ground.

Painted with broad painterly brushstrokes and flat shaded color planes in vanilla RimWorld style, with a clean, moderately thick dark outline around the whole silhouette, including every leg, the neck, the head and the feet. The hide has no fine photographic texture.

invariants: narrow torso held a man's height above the sand on four thin legs
four legs, thin and long, clearly longer than the body is deep
painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic proportions
long shadow cast from the raised body across the ground in the lower part of the sprite
sand-toned palette that suits a desert creature
each facing shows its own surface: front view with eyes toward the viewer, rear view seen from behind, side view in profile
request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite, a harrok, on a transparent background, in painterly vanilla RimWorld style with broad brushstrokes and flat shaded color planes, realistic, with a clean moderately thick dark outline around the whole silhouette including every leg. The harrok is an invented desert ambush predator. Its narrow, slab-sided torso is held a man's height above the sand on four thin, very long legs, so the legs are far longer than the body is deep. Each leg ends in a splayed, spike-like foot with three long toes gripping the sand. The hide is bare, leathery and slightly plated, in dull sand-grey and ochre with darker banding along the back, with no fur, no tuft and no hooves. A long, flexible neck bends down from the front of the torso and carries an earless, elongated skull with a narrow beak-like jaw and small sunken dark eyes set low on the sides of the head; the jaw hangs low and still just above the sand, built to pluck small animals from the shadowed ground beneath the body. The short tail is a thin bare tapering rod. The creature stands motionless in an ambush pose and casts a long, thin shadow across the ground. Front view: eyes toward the viewer, the head lowered between the front legs. Side view: profile of the narrow torso, long neck and lowered head. Rear view, seen from behind: the haunches, the tail and the back of the neck, with the eyes hidden. Nothing in the animal resembles an Earth mammal: the silhouette is a tall narrow body on four stilt legs with a down-reaching neck and head.

reasons: opus band REALLY_BAD (model said really_bad); blocking ['STYLE_EARTHLY', 'DESC_MISS', 'STYLE_OFF']; polish ['LEGIB_32']
